audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases (P) is never mentioned anywhere in either layer, and the page repeatedly tells you to spend Petrifying Gaze on his dive as though the stun will land.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby.' Petrifying Gaze is Cassiopeia's only hard CC and a 120-second cooldown. Against Mundo the first cast can be consumed by the passive without ever stopping him, and he then picks the cannister up to heal and shorten the passive's own cooldown. That single fact rewrites the level 6 advice from 'R saves you from the dive' to 'check whether his cannister is already spent before you count on the stun at all'. It is the most consequential thing missing from this matchup.
audit.corrected: The passive is now named in the level 6 spike, the wants list, whys[4], the mid text, the cooldown block, phases[4] and the key-interactions row, with the correct instruction attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infected Bonesaw is called a percent-max-HP cleaver in five places. It scales off current health, not maximum health.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'dealing damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health and slowing them.' Current-health scaling behaves the opposite way to max-health scaling in a poke war — it hits hardest when you are full and tapers as you drop, which is exactly why his early chip is scary and his finishing damage is not. Telling a Cassiopeia her max HP is the problem points her at the wrong build and the wrong risk. Its cooldown is also 4 seconds flat, which the page never says while advising you to 'trade just after he wastes it'.
audit.corrected: Changed to current-health everywhere and the 4s cooldown stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Cassiopeia five of seven stages while its own whys describe exactly two as hers and hand the last two to Mundo.
audit.why: whys[0] calls level 1 'my single clean stage'; whys[1] opens 'Skill lane'; whys[2] opens 'Even'; whys[3] opens 'Still skill'; whys[4] ends 'it stays even at best'; whys[5] says 'the lane flips to him'; whys[6] says he is unkillable and she cannot out-DPS the sustain. That is Cassiopeia, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo — which is exactly the chart in the source packet, so the win array has drifted off both the packet and the prose.
audit.corrected: win[1]=Skill, win[2]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[5]=Dr. Mundo, win[6]=Dr. Mundo, with the full-layer phase sides matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere: Heart Zapper is tracked as the matchup-defining window with no number, and Maximum Dosage is discussed as the reason the lane is lost with no number either.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and stores a portion of damage he takes, healing him off it on the burst — so unprimed Twin Fang chip during Heart Zapper is literally donated health. Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank, the same cooldown as Petrifying Gaze at rank 1, which is the concrete way to think about whether a fight at 6 is worth taking.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns added to the cooldown block, do's and all-in windows.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are skill — I can still out-chip a low-item Mundo by priming with Noxious Blast and chaining refunded Twin Fangs, and Miasma's grounding zone is my one trick to wall off his approach and his cleaver angle. But understand what 6 actually buys me: Petrifying Gaze is a panic button, not a kill button. When he flings Infected Bonesaw and walks at me, the face-check stun plus Twin Fang DPS can survive the dive, but Maximum Dosage heals through the kill window. Use R to live, not to greed — the second he finishes first item the lane inverts.

edits.before: From first item onward this is his lane and I have to be honest about it. Infected Bonesaw's percent-max-HP cleavers and his passive regen outpace my ramping Twin Fang chip, and Maximum Dosage's grey-health heal makes him unkillable longer than my boots-less, zero-resistance build stays alive. I out-poke, he out-sustains, and sustain beats poke on a drain tank every time the lane goes long. Bank the early chip lead, take plates and roam mid off my speed, and let my team's grievous wounds and burst answer him — solo, I cannot out-DPS a healing percent-HP monster who never has to walk into my Miasma.

notes: QUESTION FOR THE USER, not blocking: this page is 44.12% over 136 games, diff reads HARD, but diffRating is 4/10 and both breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t call it a 'Favoured matchup'. The prose now consistently says Cassiopeia loses the lane from first item onward, so HARD looks like the correct label and the 4/10 plus the word 'Favoured' look like the strays — the opposite of what I found on the Cho'Gath and Darius pages, where the number was right and the label was wrong. I did not guess the numeric scale, so diff, diffRating, carryRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t are all untouched here and need one ruling that moves them together. Also worth noting: Heart Zapper is a self-buff aura, not an engage tool, but the full layer frames it as the ability that 'starts the fight' — I softened that where I edited without rewriting the framing wholesale.
